caption: What if you lived on Uranus? First, the trip: Uranus is about 2.9 billion km from the Sun, so sunlight takes around 2 hours 40 minutes to get there. The planet is tipped over by about 98 degrees, so it rolls around the Sun on its side. There's no ground to land on, just clouds over a hot, dense fluid of water, methane and ammonia ices. The air can drop to -224 °C, colder than Neptune in places, and winds reach about 900 km/h, as fast as a cruising jet. Because of that tilt, each pole gets about 42 years of sunlight, then about 42 years of darkness. One Uranus year lasts 84 Earth years. With India's life expectancy around 72, most of us would never see our first Uranus birthday. Plot twist: scientists found hydrogen sulfide above its clouds, so Uranus would smell like rotten eggs (though you'd freeze long before you noticed). Would YOU visit Uranus? 👇
